claims.claim: Patients who have a known sensitivity (allergy) to amlodipine should not take the medication.
The usual adult starting dose of amlodipine is 5 mg
The usual adult starting dose of amlodipine is taken once daily
The simvastatin dose should be limited to 20 mg per day in patients who are taking amlodipine.
The most common side effect of amlodipine is edema (peripheral edema)
The over-the-counter label states that a person should not take more than 48 aspirin tablets in a 24-hour period unless a doctor directs otherwise.
Aspirin should generally not be taken during the last three months of pregnancy.
Aspirin may cause problems for the unborn child.
Aspirin may cause complications during delivery.
Aspirin may be used in late pregnancy only if a doctor specifically directs it.
The information is from an over-the-counter drug label.
Atorvastatin is contraindicated in patients who have acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
Atorvastatin is contraindicated in patients who have hypersensitivity to atorvastatin or any of its excipients
The recommended starting dose for adult patients is 10 mg or 20 mg taken once daily.
The dosage range for adult patients is 10 mg to 80 mg daily.
The prescribing information states that the recommended starting dosage in adult patients is 10 mg to 20 mg once daily.
Hemodialysis is not expected to significantly enhance clearance of atorvastatin in an overdose.
The reason hemodialysis is not expected to significantly enhance clearance is that the drug is extensively bound to plasma proteins.
Hemodialysis is unlikely to be helpful in an atorvastatin overdose.
Clopidogrel tablets are contraindicated in patients who have active pathological bleeding.
Peptic ulcer is an example of active pathological bleeding for which clopidogrel is contraindicated.
Intracranial hemorrhage is an example of active pathological bleeding for which clopidogrel is contraindicated.
Clopidogrel tablets are contraindicated in patients who have hypersensitivity to clopidogrel or any component of the product.
Anaphylaxis is an example of hypersensitivity for which clopidogrel is contraindicated.
A single 300 mg oral loading dose of clopidogrel is used in acute coronary syndrome.
The loading dose is followed by 75 mg once daily thereafter.
Concomitant use of clopidogrel with omeprazole should be avoided.
Omeprazole reduces the exposure to clopidogrel’s active metabolite.
Omeprazole diminishes clopidogrel's antiplatelet effect.
The drug-interaction section for clopidogrel advises avoiding combined use with omeprazole.
The drug-interaction section for omeprazole advises avoiding combined use with clopidogrel.
Patients with anuria should not be given furosemide.
Patients with a history of hypersensitivity to furosemide should not be given furosemide.
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are dehydration
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are reduced blood volume
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are hypotension
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are electrolyte imbalance
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are hypokalemia
The principal signs and symptoms of a furosemide overdose are hypochloremic alkalosis
The maximum recommended daily dose of ibuprofen is 3200 mg per day.
Ibuprofen tablets are contraindicated in the setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery.
Ibuprofen tablets should not be used around heart-bypass surgery.
Ibuprofen tablets are indicated for relief of the signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis.
Ibuprofen tablets are indicated for relief of mild to moderate pain.
Ibuprofen tablets are indicated for the treatment of primary dysmenorrhea.
When pregnancy is detected, lisinopril should be discontinued as soon as possible
Lisinopril is contraindicated in combination with a neprilysin inhibitor such as sacubitril
Lisinopril should not be administered within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan
The initial adult dose of lisinopril for hypertension is 10 mg taken once daily.
The recommended initial dose of lisinopril for adults with hypertension is 10 mg once a day.
Combining lisinopril with a potassium-sparing diuretic can increase the risk of hyperkalemia.
Spironolactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Amiloride is a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Triamterene is a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Serum potassium should be monitored frequently when lisinopril is used together with a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Metformin is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment
Severe renal impairment is defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²
Metformin is dialyzable
Hemodialysis can remove the drug from the body
Metformin has a clearance of up to 170 mL/min under good hemodynamic conditions
Prompt hemodialysis is recommended to remove accumulated metformin in cases of suspected lactic acidosis
The most common side effects of metformin occur in > 5% of patients.
Diarrhea is a most common side effect of metformin.
Nausea/vomiting is a most common side effect of metformin.
Flatulence is a most common side effect of metformin.
Asthenia is a most common side effect of metformin.
Indigestion is a most common side effect of metformin.
Abdominal discomfort is a most common side effect of metformin.
Headache is a most common side effect of metformin.
Metoprolol is contraindicated in severe bradycardia
Metoprolol is contraindicated in second-degree heart block
Metoprolol is contraindicated in third-degree heart block
Metoprolol is contraindicated in cardiogenic shock
Metoprolol is contraindicated in decompensated heart failure
Metoprolol is contraindicated in sick-sinus syndrome unless a permanent pacemaker is in place
The recommended starting dose of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets for heart failure is 25 mg once daily for two weeks in patients with NYHA Class II heart failure.
The recommended starting dose of metoprolol succinate extended-release tablets for heart failure is 12.5 mg once daily in patients with more severe heart failure.
The dosage-and-administration section notes that the starting dose for heart failure is 12.5 or 25 mg.
Omeprazole is contraindicated in patients receiving rilpivirine-containing products.
Concomitant use of omeprazole and rilpivirine can markedly lower rilpivirine exposure.
Concomitant use decreases rilpivirine AUC by 40%.
Concomitant use decreases rilpivirine Cmax by 40%.
Concomitant use decreases rilpivirine Cmin by 33%.
Patients with hyperkalemia should not take spironolactone.
Patients with Addison’s disease should not take spironolactone.
Patients taking eplerenone at the same time should not take spironolactone.
Warfarin is generally contraindicated in pregnancy.
Warfarin can cause fetal harm.
Warfarin can cause major congenital malformations.
Warfarin can cause fetal hemorrhage.
Warfarin can cause spontaneous abortion.
Warfarin can cause fetal mortality.
The only exception to the contraindication is for pregnant women who have mechanical heart valves and are at high risk of thromboembolism.
In cases of pregnant women with mechanical heart valves at high risk of thromboembolism, the benefits of warfarin may outweigh the risks.
Excessive anticoagulation is managed first by stopping warfarin.
Vitamin K1 may be given when needed to restore clotting.
Vitamin K1 can be administered orally.
Vitamin K1 can be administered by injection (parenterally).
If a rapid reversal is required, clinicians may use prothrombin-complex concentrate.
If a rapid reversal is required, clinicians may use fresh-frozen plasma.
If a rapid reversal is required, clinicians may use activated Factor VII.
These blood products carry additional risks.
These blood products are reserved for life-threatening bleeding.
The boxed warning for warfarin states that warfarin sodium can cause major or fatal bleeding.
The boxed warning requires regular monitoring of the INR in all treated patients.
Drugs, dietary changes, and other factors can affect INR levels achieved with warfarin therapy.
Patients should be instructed on prevention measures to minimize bleeding risk.
Patients should be instructed to report any signs or symptoms of bleeding.
Once a patient on warfarin is stable, INR should be checked periodically.
The intervals for periodic INR checks generally range from 1 to 4 weeks.
